keywords.hampi: Hampi was the majestic capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, famed for granite monuments, bazaar avenues, and boulder landscapes along the Tungabhadra.
keywords.vijayanagara: The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646 AD) was founded by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, reaching its zenith under Emperor Krishnadevaraya.
keywords.krishnadevaraya: Emperor Krishnadevaraya was a great patron of literature, art, and warfare, ruling during Hampi's golden age.
keywords.vitthala: Vitthala Temple in Hampi is famous for its iconic Stone Chariot and 56 musical granite pillars that resonate with musical tones.
keywords.musical pillars: The Saregama musical pillars of Vitthala Temple emit distinct musical notes when struck gently, sculpted from single monolithic granite blocks.
keywords.stone chariot: The Stone Chariot of Hampi is a shrine dedicated to Garuda, constructed from intricately carved granite blocks with rotating wheels.
keywords.chowka bara: Chowka Bara is an ancient cross-shaped Indian board game played with cowrie shells or dice, popular in South India since antiquity.
keywords.tungabhadra: The sacred Tungabhadra River flows through Hampi, crossed by traditional round leather coracle boats.
keywords.bazaar: Hampi's grand street bazaars were world-famous trading hubs where diamonds, rubies, and silks were traded openly.
keywords.virupaksha: Virupaksha Temple is one of the oldest functioning temples in Hampi, dedicated to Lord Shiva as Virupaksha.

general_lore: Namaste, mere aaka! Welcome to the golden empire of Vijayanagara along the sacred Tungabhadra River!
